correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, 2<=k<n, a full labelled state belongs to A or B; all safe jump rates and killing rates lump exactly into Q=[[-k,k],[r,-k]]. Matrix exponentiation gives two exact survivor functions. The positive full-state eigenfunction sqrt(k) on A and sqrt(r) on B satisfies Qh=-(k-sqrt(kr))h at every configuration. A finite-horizon Markov argument gives the Doob transformed rates s in both directions, hence a Poisson hub-switch clock. Normalized Q semigroup gives terminal Yaglom hub frequency sqrt(k)/(sqrt(k)+sqrt(r)); suppressing colliding jumps gives stationary B probability k/(k+r). Verified finite-state checker covers 50965 assertions for n=3..7, 2<=k<n; all-parameter statements rely on the analytic proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Stars are the canonical finite graphs with one bottleneck vertex: collision avoidance differs most sharply from collision suppression there. The complete family of exact survival, Poisson hub switching and three strictly ordered hub laws is a natural solvable interacting-walk benchmark for all particle counts. The exact TV difference (k-r)/(2(k+r)) tends to 1/2 along high-occupancy limits, a macroscopic observable discrepancy. This is not a low-order numerical example or merely a restatement of the general h-transform.
